headline: Highest risk is data leakage: gpt-researcher can read local files and call external APIs, while awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge list with no runtime isolation or ingestion controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime or ingestion surface, so it cannot be directly hijacked. B can read files and run browsers, so if an operator manually copies A-derived content into B, prompt injection is possible, but the bridge is manual and the blast radius is limited. Both profiles lack a shared automated channel.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from awesome-selfhosted into gpt-researcher prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared MCP or filesystem bridge is added later, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Avoid pasting untrusted list entries into B prompts.
Disable any shared MCP bridge between the pair.
Review B outputs for instruction-like text before reuse.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read local documents and send data to external APIs, while A is a knowledge-management artifact with no runtime egress. If A content or adjacent local documents are placed in B's workspace, B can transmit them off-box by default. The pair therefore creates a default leakage path for local materials, though A itself does not exfiltrate.
conditions: IF A-derived notes or local documents are stored in B's readable workspace, B can upload them to third-party APIs.
IF B is configured with external search or API backends, leakage expands beyond local-only handling.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of B's workspace.
Use a redacted copy of any A-derived material.
Restrict B to local-only sources where possible.
Rotate API keys if sensitive content was already processed.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level access controls or DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is not runnable and has no write surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can install packages and spawn subprocesses, but without a shared writable target or locking primitive in A, there is no meaningful write-write conflict between the pair. Any conflict would require an external shared directory not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or git repo, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locks or shared state, the current assessment changes.
mitigations: Do not point both agents at the same output directory.
Run B in an isolated temp workspace.
Avoid concurrent package installs during research runs.
Use separate git branches for any generated artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a research writer with planner/execution/publisher roles, so it may treat upstream material as authoritative when generating reports. A is a curated knowledge list, not a verifier, so if its entries are fed into B, errors can cascade into polished but unverified outputs. The pathway exists in default research workflows, though it is not guaranteed.
conditions: IF A-derived entries are used as source material for B reports, B can amplify mistakes.
IF B is instructed to publish without independent verification, cascading error risk rises.
mitigations: Require B to cite primary sources, not only A.
Add a verification step before publishing B outputs.
Mark A as a directory of leads, not facts.
Spot-check a sample of B's claims against originals.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking from A into B.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a public open-source knowledge-management site with no touched data classes, while B handles local documents and external research APIs. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced, but B's handling of local documents and API-backed research can create compliance obligations if sensitive data is introduced. A is not the compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B's research inputs, retention and residency controls become relevant.
IF B is used with EU PII or PHI, additional policy review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B unless approved.
Document which APIs receive which data classes.
Minimize retention of generated reports.
Use a separate tenant or account for sensitive work.
requires-engineering: add data-class routing and retention controls.
